title: Delimitation
lead: Fixing or redrawing constituency boundaries based on the latest census — aiming at ==‘one person, one vote, one value’==. The ==Delimitation Bills of 2026== (Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, Delimitation Bill, and UT Laws (Amendment) Bill) were recently ==negatived==.

items: ==Fair representation== — each vote carries equal weight; prevents over- or under-representation
==Equity== — equitable seat distribution reflecting demographic shifts
==Reserved seats== — allocation for ==SC and ST== communities
==Federal balance== — distribution of political power among states
==Level playing field== — fair geographical division so no party gains undue advantage

items.title: Population vs Federalism
bullets: States with ==higher population growth gain seats==, reducing the influence of states with ==better population control==

items.title: Political Advantage
bullets: Redrawing boundaries can advantage certain parties — ==gerrymandering== concerns

items.title: Reservation Policies
bullets: ==SC/ST reserved seat allocation== becomes contentious when boundaries change

items.title: Implementation Delays
bullets: A time-consuming process — ==up to five years==

items.title: Smaller States & UTs
bullets: Ensuring ==adequate representation== for smaller states and union territories remains a challenge

blocks.text: Delimitation is not just an arithmetic exercise of drawing lines on a map — it is a political act that redraws the contours of power, voice and equality. Should representation be a reward for growth or governance? If we mistake numerical majority for moral authority, we risk turning federalism into a formality and democracy into demography.
